subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What is the difference between a soap and a synthetic detergent?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Unit 14 (Chemistry in Everyday Life) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.105-106, printed chapter "11. CHEMISTRY IN EVERYDAY LIFE"; the book prints this question on book p.105 as VSAQ 15. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK GAP (book p.105, VSAQ 15): the printed answer gives only the hard water difference and never says what either substance is, so a student cannot say why the difference exists. What each one is chemically is added here, together with the reason: the calcium and magnesium salts of a soap are insoluble and form a scum, while the corresponding salts of a detergent are soluble. CROSS-CARD BOUNDARY: ts_ipe_c2_sc_micelle_cleaning_action, in unit 5 Surface Chemistry of this same subject, carries the micelle mechanism of cleaning. This card deliberately does not restate that mechanism; it stays on composition and hard water, which is what this question asks.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What each one is
lines: A soap is the sodium or potassium salt of
A synthetic detergent is the sodium salt
of a long chain alkyl hydrogen sulphate
or of an alkyl benzene sulphonate.
steps.why: The two substances clean in the same way, so the difference has to start from what they are made of. A soap carries a carboxylate head, and a detergent carries a sulphate or a sulphonate head; that one change of head group is the reason for every difference that follows.
common_mistakes: Writing that a detergent is a kind of soap. The head group is different, so it is a different class.
Leaving out the words long chain. Both molecules need a long hydrocarbon chain to clean.
steps.memory_tip: Soap has a carboxylate head; a detergent has a sulphate or sulphonate head.
steps.margin_note: Naming the two head groups is what earns this mark. The chain is the same in both.

steps.label: The difference in hard water
lines: Soap can be used for washing only in
In hard water the Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions form
an insoluble scum with the soap.

lines.text: Detergents clean in soft and hard water

lines: because their calcium and magnesium salts
are soluble. They also clean in acid water.
steps.why: Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions. With a soap these form calcium and magnesium salts of the fatty acid, which are insoluble and separate as a scum, so the soap is used up and does not clean. The corresponding sulphonate salts are soluble, so a detergent still cleans. A soap is also decomposed in acidic water, and a detergent is not.
common_mistakes: Writing that a soap does not dissolve in hard water. The soap dissolves; it is the calcium and magnesium salt formed from it that is insoluble.
Naming the difference with no reason. The scum is what earns this mark.
steps.memory_tip: Hard water plus soap gives an insoluble scum; hard water plus detergent gives a soluble salt.
steps.margin_note: Write the words scum and Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺. That is the difference the examiner marks.

insider_note: The book's answer is only the hard water line. Add one sentence saying that calcium and magnesium ions form an insoluble scum with soap; that reason is what turns a stated difference into an explained one.
